traps.shape: the advisory's own route: a caller-supplied custom log name is joined into a path and interpolated inside the quoted `log using "..."` command; a line break in the value ends that command and the following text runs as a new Stata command. The same value also chooses the log file's location when it contains path separators.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: None on the merits: this is the route the report names. The do-file guard reads the do-file content, which never contains the log name, so the existing protection does not cover it.
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-4P62-HQP5-G644); the documented default and custom names are the coupled values

traps.shape: a do-file path is resolve()d, existence-checked and confined to the allowed roots, then the same path text is interpolated into `do "..."`; a line break in a file name inside the allowed root ends that command and the next line runs. The checked object (the resolved path) and the interpolated object (the same lexical text) are different questions.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The boundary check already resolves the path, checks it exists and confines it to the allowed roots, so a solver reads it as a trusted path rather than caller-controlled text.

traps.shape: a help topic is interpolated into `help {cmd}` and written to a live pexpect Stata session with sendline; a newline in the topic adds a command line. It is a different package and a read-only-looking operation, so the similarity to the log wrapper is easy to miss.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Help is a read-only documentation lookup in a different MCP tool and a different package, not the do-file log wrapper the report names.

traps.shape: a package name or a net source address is interpolated into the installer command text and sent to a live pexpect session; a newline adds a command line. The same values legitimately contain separators (`user/repo`, a URL with `:` and `/`), so a shared allow-list that serves the log name breaks them.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Package installation is a separate MCP tool with its own argument surface; package names read as identifiers rather than free text, and the advisory is about the log name.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the product is a Python library whose documented error channel is a returned error entry or a raised exception, so an exception on an attacker value is a clean refusal; refuse_all.patch covers breaking legitimate calls
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected route is an action (run a do-file, look up help, install a package); there is no read/write split over the protected sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, secret or role lookup participates in these routes; the dangerous-command guard is local and does not gate the command text

A.summary: a caller-supplied log name is interpolated into the Stata log command and can run another command
